cms.title: Lindsay Davenport claimed her second Indian Wells title in 2000, defeating Elena Dementieva 6-2, 6-1 in the semifinals and Martina Hingis 4-6, 6-4, 6-0 in the final.

The only year which featured the same players in both Indian Wells and Miami finals was 2000; Martina Hingis reversed the California result 6-3, 6-2 win over Lindsay Davenport in Florida, ending a run of five straight defeats to the American (Getty)
Richard Williams, Venus Williams - Indian Wells 2001
cms.description: Venus and Richard Williams watch Serena during the 2001 Indian Wells final, throughout which the family were booed.

cms.title: Serena Williams won Indian Wells for a second time in 2001 with a brave 4-6, 6-4, 6-2 victory over Kim Clijsters in the final.
2001 Indian Wells winner Serena Williams fell to Jennifer Capriati in Miami for the second straight year, this time 6-1, 7-6(5) at the quarterfinal stage (Getty)
In 2002, shock Indian Wells champion Daniela Hantuchova couldn't sustain her momentum in Miami, falling 4-6, 6-4, 6-2 to World No.75 Cara Black in her second-round opener (Getty)

2003 Indian Wells victor Kim Clijsters powered to the Miami semifinals without conceding more than two games in any set - but once there was defeated 6-4, 6-2 by Serena Williams for the eighth time in nine meetings (Getty)
Neither 2004 Indian Wells champion Justine Henin nor runner-up Lindsay Davenport competed in Miami, with the former citing early clay-court preparation and the latter opting for some rest (Getty)
Sunshine Double: Azarenka won 2016 Indian Wells and Miami back to back, becoming just the third player after Steffi Graf (1994, 1996) and Kim Clijsters (2005) to achieve the feat. (Getty Images)

Kim Clijsters became the second ever player to complete the Sunshine Double in 2005, remarkably capturing both Indian Wells and Miami while unseeded and without a first-round bye - the latter without dropping a set (Getty)
In 2006, a young Maria Sharapova won the first of her two titles at Indian Wells, routing countrywoman Elena Dementieva in two sets. (Getty Images)
2006 Indian Wells champion Maria Sharapova made it to the Miami final when Tatiana Golovin retired in their semifinal, but fell to Svetlana Kuznetsova 6-4, 6-3 in the final (Getty)
Daniela Hantuchova won Indian Wells for a second time in 2007, and though she won a match in Miami this time the Slovak fell 6-4, 6-2 to Vera Zvonareva in the third round (Getty)
Daniela Hantuchova's first two WTA titles both came at Indian Wells as she claimed her second trophy five years after the first, defeating Svetlana Kuznetsova 6-3, 6-4 in the 2007 final.

2008 Indian Wells champion Ana Ivanovic fell 6-4, 6-2 to Lindsay Davenport, who was returning from maternity leave and ranked World No.33, in the third round of Miami - one of two Top 5 wins the American gained in her comeback (Getty)
Vera Zvonareva had defeated Li Na 6-4, 6-4 en route to the 2009 Indian Wells title in the fourth round - but fell 6-4, 3-6, 6-2 to the Chinese player in the Miami third round (Getty)

In 2010, Jelena Jankovic beat Samantha Stosur 6-2, 6-4 in the Indian Wells semifinals before claiming the title, but the Australian gained revenge 6-1, 7-6(9) in the Miami fourth round for her first win over Jankovic in four meetings (Getty)
Martina Hingis raced past Lindsay Davenport, 6-3, 6-2, to win her second Miami title in 2000.

The only year which featured the same players in both Indian Wells and Miami finals was 2000; Martina Hingis reversed the California result 6-3, 6-2 win over Lindsay Davenport in Florida, ending a run of five straight defeats to the American (Getty)

Serena Williams's first Miami title in 2002 was won without the loss of a set: the American routed 1997-2001 champions Martina Hingis 6-4, 6-0 and Venus Williams 6-2, 6-2 before overcoming Jennifer Capriati 7-5, 7-6(4) in the final (Getty)

cms.title: Belgium’s Kim Clijsters beat Maria Sharapova, 6-3, 7-5 to take the 2005 Miami crown.
Kim Clijsters proved too strong for Venus Williams in the 2010 final, winning 6-2, 6-1. It was the second time she had won the crown, adding to her 2005 Miami title.
Sunshine Double: Azarenka won 2016 Indian Wells and Miami back to back, becoming just the third player after Steffi Graf (1994, 1996) and Kim Clijsters (2005) to achieve the feat. (Getty Images)

Kim Clijsters became the second ever player to complete the Sunshine Double in 2005, remarkably capturing both Indian Wells and Miami while unseeded and without a first-round bye - the latter without dropping a set (Getty)

Kim Clijsters completed a remarkable Sunshine Double in 2005 on her return from a wrist injury, becoming the lowest-ranked (at World No.38) and first unseeded player to win the Miami title with a 6-3, 7-5 win over Maria Sharapova in the final (Getty)
2006 Indian Wells champion Maria Sharapova made it to the Miami final when Tatiana Golovin retired in their semifinal, but fell to Svetlana Kuznetsova 6-4, 6-3 in the final (Getty)

Russians Rising: Three Russians had previously fallen in the Miami final, but 2006 saw the new generation make their mark on the tour, with Svetlana Kuznetsova beating Maria Sharapova in Miami’s first all-Russian final. (Getty Images)

Svetlana Kuznetsova saved a match point against Martina Hingis to win their 2006 third-rounder 3-6, 6-1, 7-6(9), then stormed to the title without dropping another set, winning the only all-Russian Miami final to date over Maria Sharapova 6-4, 6-3 (Getty)
Serena Williams, Miami 2007
Jelena Jankovic has gone very far in Miami before - she was runner-up to Serena Williams in 2008.
Victoria Azarenka, Miami 2009 (Getty)
Victoria Azarenka & Serena Williams, Miami 2009
Serena Williams and Victoria Azarenka ahead of the 2009 Miami final (Getty)
Serena Williams and Victoria Azarenka ahead of the 2009 Miami final (Getty)
Serena Williams and Victoria Azarenka ahead of the 2009 Miami final (Getty)
Victoria Azarenka is no stranger to winning in Miami - she has won it two times, in 2009 and 2011.
Victoria Azarenka is the only woman to have beaten Serena in a Miami final to date. She won 6-3, 6-1 in 2009.
Victoria Azarenka became a two-time Miami champion in 2011, defeating Maria Sharapova, 6-1, 6-4, in the final. Azarenka won the event two years prior, defeating Serena Williams in the 2009 final.
A few weeks later, Serena took revenge 6-4, 3-6, 6-3 in the 2009 Miami semifinals to end World No.6 Venus's 13-match winning streak - but the World No.1 would lose the final to Victoria Azarenka.

Victoria Azarenka won her third title and first at Premier level at Miami 2009, coming through a 6-3, 2-6, 7-5 against Svetlana Kuznetsova in the semifinals before ending Serena Williams's quest for a second hat-trick 6-3, 6-1 in the final (Getty)
Kim Clijsters proved too strong for Venus Williams in the 2010 final, winning 6-2, 6-1. It was the second time she had won the crown, adding to her 2005 Miami title.
After a nine-year absence from the Miami final, Venus returned in 2010 with wins over Agnieszka Radwanska and Marion Bartoli - but fell 6-2, 6-1 to Kim Clijsters at the last hurdle (Getty)

Kim Clijsters took her second Miami trophy in 2010, dethroning Victoria Azarenka 6-4, 6-0 in round four, edging Justine Henin 6-2, 6-7(3), 7-6(6) in the SFs and capturing her third post-maternity title 6-2, 6-1 over Venus Williams in the final (Getty)

The USA's Monica Seles lost only 10 games in four matches en route to the Sydney 2000 semifinals and, after falling 6-1, 4-6, 6-3 to compatriot Venus Williams, dismissed home favorite Jelena Dokic 6-1, 6-4 to seal bronze.

Dinara Safina ended the hopes of two home players, Zheng Jie in the third round and Li Na in the semifinals, as well as defeating No.2 seed Jelena Jankovic in the quarterfinals, en route to capturing silver at Beijing 2008.
Dinara Safina, Rome 2009

Dinara Safina continued to sweep through the 2009 clay season, adding the Madrid trophy to her Rome title with a 6-2, 6-4 win over Caroline Wozniacki in the final - the only time the pair ever faced off.

Victories over Lucie Safarova, Alona Bondarenko and Patty Schnyder extended Dinara Safina's winning streak to nine, putting the Russian into her third straight final (following Stuttgart and Rome) and fifth of the 2009 season.
Three-time Slam finalist Dinara Safina rose to No.1 off the back of a 38-6 record in the summer of 2009, and scored 26 weeks in the top spot in total (Getty)

cms.title: Unseeded Aravane Rezaï sprung a surprise in 2010 to claim the title in Madrid, defeating Venus Williams, 6-2, 7-5 in the final. (Getty)

Justine Henin came into Madrid fresh off the first title of her 2010 comeback in Stuttgart, but Aravane Rezai sprung a first-round shock, reeling off the last eight games for a 4-6, 7-5, 6-0 win - a foreshadowing of how the tournament would pan out.
